This video program will show your technicians a method of roughing a thread with a single point tool and then finishing it with a die. This method may not produce a thread as precise as a machined thread but it is a fast and productive way to make two parts fit together.
Machining offset holes (face plate and four-jaw chuck)

The term "offset" refers to any machining operation that cannot by performed in a self-aligning 3-jaw chuck concentric to the workpiece. In this video program, you will be shown two methods of machining offset holes in a work piece on the engine lathe.

The primary means of communication between designers and manufacturers is the blueprint. Over the years, these blueprints have evolved in substance and style. They're not as simple as they once were. When your technicians have completed this course, they will be able to describe the need for Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing Standards, define Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing and differentiate it from the "Coordinate Dimensioning Method," identify the key principles and advantages of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing and define nominal size, actual size, tolerance, bilateral tolerance, unilateral tolerance, limits of size and limit dimensioning.

Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing is a symbolic language used to communicate manufacturing operations instead of designer notes on drawings. This presentation introduces the basic symbols and abbreviations that are used in this language. After completing this course, your technicians will be able to interpret symbols used to identify geometric characteristics and abbreviations, define impoiirtant terms relating to GD&T and explain the material modifiers MMC, LMC and RFS.

There are many general symbols associated with Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing. This program will introduce your technicians to datums. When they complete the course, they will be able to describe the concept of datums, identify the datum feature symbol, define the datum reference frame concept for both circular and non-circular parts and identify datum targets

This program introduces the interpretation of geometric form controls. When you have completed this program you will be able to interpret and apply the specific tolerance for straightness, flatness, circularity and cylindricity. You will also be able to interpret the application of Per Unit Control.

The advantages of using Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing become apparent when it is used to control form and orientation tolerances on irregularly shaped parts. When you have completed this program, you will be able to describle the applications of profile of a line, profile of a surface, circular runout and total runout.

This program introduces the student to the concepts of virtual condition and resultant condition. These conditions ensure interchangeability of parts within an assembly. Interchageability becomes an important issue today when components are manufactured in one country and assembled in another. When you have completed this course, you will be able to define virtual and resultant condition and calculatre these conditions for features.

A finished product is often composed of many parts which must mate with one another. To ensure a precise fit between mating parts and their features, location tolerancing is used as an effecitve tool of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing. After completing this course, you will be able to describe location tolerancing, explain position tolerancing, define a projected tolerancing and explain composite positional tolerancing.

This program shows that position tolerances are not arbitrary numbers pulled out of a hat. Rather, they are calculated values based on the actual size of the mating features on the respective parts including the fasteners themselves. When you have completed this program, you will be able to identify and calculate position tolerances for floating fastener application, fixed fastener applications and three piece assemblies.

In this presentation, you will learn what feature control frames are, how to read them and how they are used.

GD&T, like any other standard or practice, has rules that play an important part in the standard. These rules also control certain drafting practices and provide guidelines for designers as well as readers of drawings. This program will teach your technicians how to define the basic rules of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing and how to apply the basic principles involved.

This program deals with angularity and parallelism. When you have completed this presentation you will be able to identify and interpret the methods of specifiying both angularity and parallelism and describe how they may affect orientation.

Location tolerancing is used to ensure the precise fit between mating parts and their features. This program introduces additional methods of location tolerancing. After completing the program, you will be able to describe coaxility and concentricity and define bi-directional positional tolerancing.
Grinding forming tools and machining forms

Machinists are constantly required to cut grooves or shapes into cylindrical work pieces. This operation is called "grooving" or "necking." This video program will teach your technicians how to grind forming tools and machine grooves and shapes on a cylinder using forming tools.

Parting, or cutting-off, is the process of cutting a groove around a revolving workpiece to sever it from the piece held in the lathe. This video program will demonstrate the proper procedures for parting or cutting-off on the engine lathe.

This video program will show an operation the machinist performs frequently -- cutting external threads on the engine lathe. This demonstration will show how to cut one of the most common forms of screw thread -- the unified, a sixty degree and V-type threads.
The Acme thread is generally larger and coarser than the V-thread. This video program will demonstrate how to cut Acme threads on the lathe.
A tapered pipe thread permits a tighter connection than would be possible with a straight thread. This video program will demonstrate how to machine, or chase, tapered pipe threads.
